To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inhibition of muscle carbonic-anhydrase slows the calcium transient in rat skeletal-muscle fibers.
inhibition of SR carbonic an hydrase decelerates the Ca(2 +) transient and contraction time in skeletal muscle fibers of rats.
the inhibition of SR- CA by the lipophilic inhibitors L-64551, chlorzolamid, and ethoxzolidamid slows the kinetics of intracellular Ca2+ transients and contraction of skeletal muscle fibers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of carbonic anhydrases (CAs) in skeletal muscle.
the role of carbonic anhydrases (CA) in muscle contraction and relaxation.
the role of the carbonic anhydrases of the sarcoplasmatic reticulum in the regulation of the Ca(2+),H(+) homeostasis of the muscle cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SR-CA is a rate-limiting enzyme for the SR H(+) pump, which is essential for the Ca(2+), and therefore the force, transient.
SR-CA accelerates H(+) flux across the SR membrane and that this acceleration is essential to accelerate the rate of Ca(2+)(2+) transport across SR membrane.
SR-CA accelerates Ca(2+) release by increasing the rate of HCO(-) formation and thus the rate of H(+)-ion production in the SR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inhibition of SR CA decelerates the Ca(2+)+HCO(-)(3) reaction in the SR, which then slows the rate of H(+)-Ca(2+) exchange and the Ca(2)+ release from the SR.
SR-CA is a key enzyme for the fast relaxation of Ca(2+).
inhibition of SR carbonic an hydrase slows down the Ca(2+)+-transient in rat skeletal muscle fibres.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SR-CA is an essential component of Ca(2+)(i) regulation and contraction in skeletal muscle.
SR-CA is a critical regulator of Ca(2+), H(+), and force transients in skeletal muscle.
the SR CA is a critical component in the regulation of intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis and muscle contraction.
